audit.why: Camille owns level 1 (Precision Protocol empowered auto plus the Adaptive Defenses shield against an Akali with one Q), Akali owns 3 through first item once Twilight Shroud can eat Hookshot, and Camille owns 6 and the two-item split-push game. The mirror audits/top/camille__akali.json labels the same stages the same way from her side.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 and Level 6 phase text were the generic template and named neither ultimate nor cooldown.
audit.why: Level 1 is decided by Precision Protocol: it is an auto-attack reset (9s at rank 1, 325 range) whose recast does significantly more damage if she delays between the two attacks — that is the burst tell flagged in _missing/akali.json. Level 6 is The Hextech Ultimatum, 140s at rank 1, which Riot's text says anchors the target to the area; the mirror confirms the dash grants no immunity and that she spends it once Twilight Shroud is gone.
audit.corrected: The Hextech Ultimatum (140s) anchors you inside its zone — your R will not carry you out, so bait her E first.

audit.whatIsWrong: Key Ability Interactions said only "Track Camille's Hookshot: her engage/stun, shroud-dodge it" and stated no interaction. Three of the four interactions flagged for this matchup were absent entirely.
audit.why: Adaptive Defenses gives her a shield sized to a percentage of her max health against the damage type that hit her — she autos you once and your magic burst lands into a magic shield, so it has to be forced out first. Hookshot requires a wall to pull to (16/15/14/13/12) and knocks up on landing, so away from terrain she has no engage. Tactical Sweep's outer half slows, deals extra damage and heals her, which is the anti-heal trigger.
audit.corrected: Adaptive Defenses shields her against magic when she autos you — force it out before you burst.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two Don't descriptions did not explain their own titles: "Get E-stunned into her combo" was explained as "that is Camille's favourite window", and "Fight near walls" as "burning it for tiny value leaves you naked".
audit.why: The titles are the right mistakes and the kit explains both: Hookshot knocks up on landing and leads into the true-damage Q recast, and Hookshot only functions off terrain.
audit.corrected: Hookshot (16s) only works off terrain — in the open she has no engage.

notes: Both suspectNames for this matchup are false positives. Content layer already names the real kit and is at bar quality; the second cast of her E is called Wall Dive there, which the kit file does not list (it only carries "Hookshot") — left alone rather than corrected, since Riot's own description does describe the two-stage pull-and-leap. Not claimed because it is not in the data: whether Perfect Execution, Flash or Twilight Shroud's untargetability can break The Hextech Ultimatum's anchor. The edit says only that R will not carry you out, which follows from Riot's wording and matches the mirror.
